title: Pasting tower maps with the additive Roos comparisons
statement: Let A,B,D be abelian categories with countable products, F:A→B,G:B→D,H:A→D additive functors and a:H≅F⋙G. Let C,Cf,Cc,Chf be strict cochain towers in A,B,D,D. Let fRoos,gRoos,hRoos be maps with the same sources and targets as scalarRoosMap(F,C), scalarRoosMap(G,Cf), scalarRoosMap(H,C) [def-sf-additive-roos-map], and assume each equals that canonical map. Let rF:C⋙FC→Cf, rG:Cf⋙GC→Chf, rH:C⋙HC→Cc, sigma:Cc→Chf be tower maps, where FC,GC,HC denote the induced cochain functors. Let alpha:HC→FC⋙GC be the cochain transformation of a.hom. Assume rH≫sigma=whiskerLeft(C,alpha)≫whiskerRight(rF,GC)≫rG. For the strict Roos functor [def-sf-strict-roos-functor], alpha_(Roos C)≫GC(fRoos)≫GC(Roos(rF))≫gRoos≫Roos(rG) = hRoos≫Roos(rH)≫Roos(sigma). No invertibility of the tower maps or of the three Roos comparisons is required.

source.place: Steps 1 and 5: identity and composition of the normalized quotient, Roos-limit and tensor transport.

proof.text: Replace fRoos,gRoos,hRoos by the canonical maps. Naturality of scalarRoosMap(G) at rF replaces GC(Roos(rF)) followed by scalarRoosMap(G,Cf) with scalarRoosMap(G,C⋙FC) followed by Roos(whiskerRight(rF,GC)). Apply additive Roos composition to the three leading factors. The left side is now scalarRoosMap(H,C) followed by the Roos image of whiskerLeft(C,alpha)≫whiskerRight(rF,GC)≫rG. Substitute the assumed tower equation backwards and use Roos functoriality. This is exactly the right side.

theorem podCompositionRoosPasting
    {A B D : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [Category D]
    [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [Abelian D]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [HasCountableProducts B] [HasCountableProducts D]
    (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ D) (H : A ⥤ D)
    [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [H.Additive] (a : H ≅ F ⋙ G)
    (C : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ) (Cf : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex B ℤ)
    (Cc Chf : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex D ℤ)
    (fRoos : (F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (integralOperationsRoos C) ⟶
      integralOperationsRoos (C ⋙ F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)))
    (gRoos : (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (integralOperationsRoos Cf) ⟶
      integralOperationsRoos (Cf ⋙ G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)))
    (hRoos : (H.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (integralOperationsRoos C) ⟶
      integralOperationsRoos (C ⋙ H.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)))
    (rF : C ⋙ F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶ Cf)
    (rG : Cf ⋙ G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶ Chf)
    (rH : C ⋙ H.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶ Cc) (σ : Cc ⟶ Chf)
    (hf : fRoos = scalarRoosMap F C) (hg : gRoos = scalarRoosMap G Cf)
    (hh : hRoos = scalarRoosMap H C) :
    let α : H.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶
        F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙ G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) :=
      NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex a.hom (.up ℤ)
    rH ≫ σ = whiskerLeft C α ≫
        whiskerRight rF (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)) ≫ rG →
    α.app (integralOperationsRoos C) ≫
        (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map fRoos ≫
        (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (integralOperationsRoosFunctor.map rF) ≫
        gRoos ≫ integralOperationsRoosFunctor.map rG =
      hRoos ≫ integralOperationsRoosFunctor.map rH ≫
        integralOperationsRoosFunctor.map σ
